claim: The conditional emission excludes netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework even though ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on both. Generated code for those supported targets therefore has no active attribute, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be decorated; conditional emission is only justified where the attribute is unavailable.

receipt_plan.detail: Run generator tests with parse options defining NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK, compiling against netstandard2.0 and net462 reference assemblies respectively, and assert that every generated class has an active ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute. On HEAD the guarded attributes are absent. In the same target compilations, compile a source class directly decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute to establish that removing the guard is valid.

claim: An unrelated change formats decimals with StandardFormat('F'). Fixed-point formatting without an explicit precision rounds to the framework's default number of decimal places, so values such as 0.001m can be serialized as "0.00" and 1.234m as "1.23", losing data and changing the stable wire representation. This is outside the code-coverage feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Using base-built and head-built MessagePack assemblies, serialize 0.001m and 1.234m with MessagePackSerializer.Serialize<decimal> under the same default options, compare the MessagePack string payload bytes, and round-trip the HEAD payload. BASE preserves "0.001" and "1.234"; HEAD emits fixed-format rounded strings and round-trips different numeric values.

claim: The new fixed-point StandardFormat('F') has no explicit precision, so decimal formatting uses the fixed-point default of two fractional digits. Consequently, serializing 123.456m produces a string rounded to 123.46, and deserialization returns a different value instead of preserving the decimal.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.DecimalFixedPointFormattingReceiptTests.DecimalSerializationPreservesFractionalValue in tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/DecimalFixedPointFormattingReceiptTests.cs. It round-trips 123.456m through MessagePackSerializer and asserts equality; on head the rounded fixed-point representation fails the assertion.

claim: The decimal formatter now uses the fixed-point 'F' format without a precision specifier, whose default is two fractional digits. Values such as 123.456m therefore serialize as "123.46" instead of "123.456", changing the established wire bytes and losing data on deserialization; this unrelated change is not required by the code-coverage feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Using otherwise identical serializers built from base and head, serialize decimal values 123.456m, 0.005m, and 1.2300m with DecimalFormatter (via MessagePackSerializer.Serialize<decimal> under the standard resolver). Compare the MessagePack string bytes and deserialize each head payload to confirm that 123.456m becomes 123.46m.
